title: Services: programs that keep running
text: Services: programs that keep running A service starts, does its work for days or months, and stops cleanly when told to: a file watcher, a job that syncs data every five minutes, a backup at night, later a web API. Pastel.Service takes care of the parts every such program needs; you write the work. A service Run does, in order: 1. read the settings: Configure gives the defaults, then /etc/<name /config.toml , ~/.config/<name /config.toml , ./config.toml and the environment data.md data.md . A mistake in them ends the start with exit code 1 and the reason. 2. call Started . An exception there ends the service with exit code 1 and is logged . 3. run the jobs when they are due, until the service is told to stop 4. call Stopping , log "stopped", return 0 Jobs Every Seconds, @Job, 'name' Every so many seconds fractions are fine , the first time after one interval Every Seconds, @Job, 'name', True The same, and once right at the start DailyAt '03:30', @Job, 'name' Once a day, local time A job can be a method of the service @Service.Sync or a plain procedure. Jobs run one after the other, in the main thread, so they never run at the same time and need no locks. A job that raises is logged with its name sync failed: connection refused and runs again next time; the service goes on. The next run is planned from when a job starts, so a slow job does not pile up runs. A long job should check IsStopping now and then, and wait with Wait Ms instead of Sleep : Wait returns False at once when the service is told to stop. Background work: Pastel.Workers Work that should not hold up a web request or the jobs sending mail, resizing images, calling a slow service goes to a pool of worker threads: Messages are strings JSON is handy , so threads never share objects by accident. An exception in a handler is logged worker mail: ... and counted in Failed ; the worker goes on. Submit returns False after Stop , and when the queue is full: TWorkerPool.Create 'mail', 4, @SendMail, 1000 keeps at most 1000 waiting. Pending , Processed and Failed tell how it goes for /health or the log ; WaitIdle waits until everything is done tests . Stop and Free waits for the queued work; after 30 s it logs a warning and keeps waiting. Give systemd enough time: TimeoutStopSec= in the unit. Work in the queue is in memory: it is lost when the program is killed. For work that must survive a crash, store it in the database first and let a job pick it up. TMessageQueue alone passes messages between any threads: Push , Pop Msg, TimeoutMs and Close . Stopping, reloading Ctrl+C, kill , systemctl stop , docker stop SIGINT, SIGTERM Finishes the running job, calls Stopping , ends with 0 A second Ctrl+C Ends at once systemctl reload , kill HUP SIGHUP Reads the settings again; then calls Reloaded Service.Stop , Service.Reload The same from code a job, a thread, a test When the new settings have a mistake, the old ones stay and the reason is logged. Settings in log level , format take effect at once: On Windows, Ctrl+C and closing the console window stop the service cleanly; there is no reload restart it instead . Running as a real Windows service the Services control panel is planned. Under systemd pastel new service writes deploy/<name .service and deploy/README.md with the steps to install it on a server. The unit uses: Type=notify : Pastel tells systemd when the service is ready, reloading and stopping, so systemctl start waits until Started is done and reports a failed start. ExecReload=/bin/kill HUP $MAINPID : systemctl reload applies new settings. WatchdogSec=60 commented out : when set, Pastel tells systemd every half interval that it is alive; if the main loop hangs a job stuck longer than that , systemd restarts the service. DynamicUser=yes and StateDirectory=<name : the service runs as its own user and may write only to /var/lib/<name . In code that folder is Service.StateDir ./data while developing . Logs go to the journal with their level, so journalctl u <name p err shows

title: Web APIs and sites: Pastel.Web
text: Web APIs and sites: Pastel.Web An HTTP server for JSON APIs, small web sites and health checks, in the same program as the rest of your code. examples/notes api is a complete example: an API with a web page, run as a service. pastel new api myapi makes a new API project with a database database.md database.md : models, controllers, migrations and tests. pastel new site mysite makes a web site with pages from templates and Bootstrap pages.md pages.md . A web service TWebService is a service services.md : it reads its settings, starts the server in Started , stops it cleanly on Ctrl+C or systemctl stop , and under systemd says when it is ready. The settings: Without a service, the server works on its own too: Routes Web.Get '/users', @List also Post , Put , Patch , Delete /users/:id :id matches one part of the path: Req.Param 'id' /files/ matches the rest: Req.Param ' ' is a/b/c.txt Web.Static '/', 'public' the files in a folder: /app.css → public/app.css , / → public/index.html Web.Health '/health', AppVersion {"status":"ok","version":"1.0.0","uptime seconds":..., "requests":...} Routes are tried in the order they were added. A static folder only answers when the file exists, so routes added after Static '/', ... still work. Paths in a static folder cannot leave it .. gives 404 . HEAD requests are answered like GET , without the body. A path that matches no route gets 404 {"error": "no route for GET /x"} ; one that matches with another method gets 405 with an Allow header. The request: TWebRequest Req.Method , Req.Path , Req.Body , Req.ClientIP Req.Param 'id' , Req.ParamInt 'id' parts of the path Req.Query 'q', Default , Req.QueryInt 'page', 1 , Req.HasQuery 'all' ?q=...&page=2&all Req.Header 'Authorization' any request header Req.Json , Req.JsonObject the body as JSON it belongs to the request: do not free it Req.Form 'name' a field of a submitted HTML form ParamInt , QueryInt , Json and JsonObject answer 400 with a clear message by themselves when the client sends something wrong: {"error": "id must be a whole number, not \"abc\""} . The response: TWebResponse Res.Json Data, 201 sends a TJSONData and frees it Res.JsonText '{"ok":true}' JSON you already have as text Res.Text S , Res.Html S UTF 8 text Res.SendFile FileName a file, with its content type and Last Modified ; a Range request gets that part 206 : players seek in videos, downloads go on Res.Redirect '/new', 301 Res.NoContent 204; also what a handler that sends nothing answers Res.Error 422, 'title is required' {"error": "title is required"} Res.SetHeader Name, Value The status is 200 unless given. Errors In the handler The client gets raise EWebError.Create 404, 'no user with this id' 404 {"error": "no user with this id"} a bad number, bad JSON 400 with the reason any other exception 500 {"error": "internal error"} , and the exception in the log In debug builds pastel run the 500 answer also contains the exception's message, which helps while developing; release builds never show it to clients. Filters: code that runs before the handlers Filters run in the order they were added, after the route was found and before its handler. A filter stops the request by raising EWebError or by answering itself Res.Error ... ; otherwise the next filter and then the handler run. Req.Values passes things on: Req.Values.Values 'user' := ... in a filter, read in the handler. Who is calling: API keys and tokens API keys , for programs that call your API: The caller sends X API Key: <key or Authorization: Bearer <key ; without a key or with a wrong one the answer is 401. Keys are compared in constant time, and must be at least 16 characters: make them with RandomToken Pastel.Crypto or openssl rand base64 32 , and keep them in the settings or an environment variable, never in the code. JWT , for users who log in: Requests under /api then need Authorization: Bearer <token ; the handlers read Req.Claim 'sub' , Req.Claim 'role' or Req.Claims . A forged, changed or expired token gets 401

title: WebSockets: Pastel.WebSocket
text: WebSockets: Pastel.WebSocket A WebSocket is a connection that stays open: the server can send something at any moment — a new message in a chat, an appointment booked on another phone, a price that changed — and the app sees it at once, without asking every few seconds. On the server A TWebSockets holds the clients connected to one address of a web server web.md : The filters of the address run first, like for a route: RequireJwt , RequireApiKey , RateLimit , Use . A client without a token gets 401 and no connection. Socket.Params the route's :room , Socket.Query ?name=... , Socket.Claims / Socket.Claim 'sub' the JWT and Socket.Values what the filters set, and what the program keeps about the client tell who it is. Sending: Socket.Send Text , Socket.SendJson Obj , Socket.SendBinary Bytes ; to many: Broadcast Text to all , SendTo 'user', '42', Text to the clients whose Values 'user' is 42 : one user's phone and computer, a room , SendToId Id, Text . From anywhere in the server, also from a route: POST /appointments saves and then tells the salon's other devices. OnClose : the client left Socket.CloseCode : 1000 normal, 1001 going away, 1006 the network . Socket.Close ends a connection from the server. Each client has its own thread, like requests: what the handlers share must be protected TCriticalSection . An error in a handler is logged; the connection stays. Pings every PingInterval seconds 30 keep connections alive through proxies and end those of phones that went away without a word; a message longer than MaxMessageSize 1 MB closes the connection. Stop of the server ends every connection 1001 . Web pages of other sites may not connect when Cors lists the allowed ones the Origin must be among them . A plain request to the address gets 426 and a message that it is a WebSocket. Behind nginx, the address needs proxy http version 1.1; , proxy set header Upgrade $http upgrade; and proxy set header Connection "upgrade"; deploy.md deploy.md https a reverse proxy in front ; Caddy passes WebSockets by itself. In an app Connect connects and does the handshake EWebSocketError with the reason: the server is not there, 401 , a certificate that is not trusted ; then messages come by themselves. OnMessage , OnBinary and OnClose run on the app's thread, like a button's click EventsOnAppThread := False : on the reading thread, for programs without forms . After OnClose , Connect again connects anew: a phone that lost the network does it when it is back. wss:// checks the server's certificate like HTTPS. On Android the phone's own TLS is used nothing to install . Headers adds lines to the handshake; Free closes the connection. In tests The client works against a server in the same test program: start a TWebServer on a free port, connect a TWebSocketClient with EventsOnAppThread := False , send, and wait for what comes back the framework's websocket test.pas does this .

title: E-mail: Pastel.Mail
text: E mail: Pastel.Mail Messages sent with SMTP: a password reset, an invoice, a reminder of an appointment. Any mail server works — your own, a mail service Amazon SES, Mailgun, SendGrid, Brevo , or a mailbox with an app password Gmail, Outlook . Messages With Text and Html both, mail programs show the one they can; names, subjects and texts in any language are encoded for mail UTF 8 . From of the message, if set, is used instead of the mailer's. TLS and passwords security "auto" default port 465: TLS from the start; else STARTTLS when the server offers it — and it must when there is a password "tls" TLS from the start port 465 "starttls" plain, then STARTTLS; a server without it is refused "none" never TLS: a mail server on the same computer or private network The server's certificate is checked like HTTPS's system.md system.md . With "auto" a password never goes over a connection that is not encrypted: a server without STARTTLS gets an error instead. On Android the phone's own TLS is used. Errors ESmtpError says what went wrong and what the server answered: Sending takes a moment seconds with a slow server : in a web server it runs in the request's thread; in an app, send from a worker Pastel.Workers so the window does not wait. While developing, and in tests Without host , a message is not sent: it is written to the log, so a program can be developed without a mail server. In tests CaptureMails keeps the messages instead of sending them:

title: Web pages from templates
text: Web pages from templates Pastel.Pages makes HTML pages from templates, in the style of Laravel's Blade: a layout around every page, sections, loops and conditions, values made safe for HTML. A web site is a web service web.md whose handlers answer with pages. ! The site that "pastel new site" makes, with Bootstrap images/site.png A new site src/main.pas the service: settings and the web server src/webpages.pas the pages: one handler for each address views/layouts/main.html the frame of every page: Bootstrap, the menu, the footer views/partials/nav.html the menu views/home.html , about.html , contact.html the pages the contact form is checked on the server public/ files served as they are, under /static/ : css/site.css , pictures tests/webpages test.pas the pages tested through real HTTP A saved template shows at the next reload of the page; a Pascal change needs pastel run again or pastel run watch . In VS Code: New Project… → Server → Web Site . A page View Name, Data reads views/products.html 'shop.list' is views/shop/list.html , fills it with the data — a JSON object, freed by View — and gives the HTML. Templates are read once and again when their file changes. Templates Values A missing value is empty. {{ ... }} is a comment it is not sent . @{{ x }} writes {{ x }} itself, for JavaScript frameworks. Conditions Conditions: == , != , < , <= , , = , and && , or , not ! , brackets, texts in quotes, numbers, true , false , null . Empty texts, 0 , false , null and empty lists count as false. {{ paid ? 'Paid' : 'Open' }} chooses a value. Loops In a loop: loop.index from 0 , loop.iteration from 1 , loop.first , loop.last , loop.count . Layouts, sections and partials views/layouts/main.html : views/products.html : A page fills the sections of its layout a layout can extend another layout ; text outside the sections is not shown. @include 'partials.nav' puts another template in, with the same data. @yield 'title', 'Shop' shows Shop when no page fills the section. Filters Your own: a function of a text and an argument. A form The site's contact page shows the pattern: on mistakes, the page again with the messages and what was typed status 422 ; otherwise thanks. Files, folders and servers View finds views/ next to the program on a server , in the folder it runs in pastel run , or in the project when the program is in build/ . SetViewsFolder sets another one; FindAppFolder 'public' finds public/ the same way for Web.Static '/static', ... . pastel package puts views/ and public/ into the package package include in pastel.toml , and deploy/<name .service runs the site on a Linux server deploy.md deploy.md . Without files: RenderPage Template, Data fills a template given as text; TPages.Create Folder gives a set of templates of your own Render , RenderText . Mistakes A mistake in a template stops the page with the file and the line: products 12 : @endforeach is missing , home 3 : there is no filter "money" . The web server answers with status 500 and writes the message to the log.

title: Markdown
text: Markdown Pastel.Markdown turns Markdown into HTML the way GitHub shows it: CommonMark with tables, ~~strikethrough~~, task lists and bare links. Use it for help pages, blog posts, README files shown in an app, or a whole documentation site — Pastel's website https://github.com/azrov/pastel/tree/main/tools/website is made with it and Pastel.Pages pages.md . Markdown to HTML In a web page, put it in with {!! !!} so it is not escaped a second time: HTML in the Markdown stays as it is as on GitHub , so Markdown written by visitors of a site needs cleaning first; Markdown you wrote yourself does not. What it understands Markdown HTML Title … Small <h1 id="title" … with GitHub's ids strong , em , em , ~~del~~ <strong , <em , <del code and fenced code with a language pascal <code , <pre <code class="language pascal" text address "title" , ! alt picture.png links and pictures <https://example.com , https://example.com links item , 1. item , nested lists, x done lists, task boxes quote <blockquote tables with : : alignment <table <hr two spaces or \ at the end of a line <br \ a that is not emphasis Headings and their ids Every heading gets the id GitHub gives it, so links like page.html getting started work as they do on GitHub: lower case, punctuation left out, spaces as , a second heading with the same text gets 1 . Links of your own TMarkdown gives a say over every link and picture address, and tells which ids the headings got. A documentation site makes links to .md files links to .html pages: Pastel's website tools/website in the repository is a Pastel console program that makes the website: the home page, the download page and every page of the documentation, with a menu, a search and On this page . It checks every link between pages and every anchor , so a broken link stops the tests.

title: Databases: Pastel.Db
text: Databases: Pastel.Db SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL/MariaDB with one small API. Rows come back as JSON, ready to send from a web handler. pastel new api makes a complete project with it: models, controllers, migrations and tests. Which database Address sqlite:data/app.db a file; the folder is created. Nothing to install on Linux libsqlite3 sqlite::memory: in memory, gone when the program ends tests postgres://user:password@host:5432/name PostgreSQL libpq mysql://user:password@host:3306/name MySQL or MariaDB libmysqlclient or libmariadb Keep the address in the settings, never in the code: database url = "..." in config.toml, or the environment variable MYAPP DATABASE URL . Messages and logs show it without the password Db.SafeUrl : postgres://user: @host/name . SQLite is set up for servers: waits up to 5 s when another connection writes, WAL journal, foreign keys on. Start with SQLite; move to PostgreSQL when several servers share the data. The same code and migrations work on all three. Queries Db.Query SQL, values all rows: TJSONArray of TJSONObject Db.QueryOne SQL, values the first row, or nil Db.QueryValue SQL, values , Default the first column of the first row, as text Db.QueryInt SQL, values , Default the same as a number: select count ... Db.Exec SQL, values update, delete, create table...: the number of rows changed Db.Insert SQL, values an insert: the id of the new row You free what Query and QueryOne return, or hand it to Res.Json , which frees it. Columns become JSON values: numbers, text, true / false on PostgreSQL; SQLite and MySQL give 0 / 1 , and null . Values always go in as ? . They are sent apart from the SQL, so a name like x' ; drop table users; is stored as a name and can never change the query. Never build SQL from user input with + or Format . Errors EDbDuplicate a unique column already has this value: answer 409 EDbError anything else: bad SQL the message shows the SQL , cannot connect, wrong number of ? Transactions A transaction has the same query functions as Db . Threads One TDatabase serves the whole program, including every web request at the same time: it keeps a pool of connections 10 unless TDatabase.Open Url, 20 . Open it once when the program starts. Migrations: the tables The tables are made by SQL files in database/migrations , run in name order, each once: {{id}} becomes the auto numbered key of each database integer primary key autoincrement , bigserial primary key , bigint auto increment primary key , so one file works everywhere. Db.Migrate in the program does the same when it starts, so a new version on the server brings its tables along. Each file runs in a transaction on MySQL, create / alter cannot be undone: keep one change per file . The table schema migrations records what ran. Never change a migration after it ran somewhere ; add a new one. Models: where the SQL lives pastel new api puts all SQL of a table in one class, the model src/models/tasks.pas ; the controllers src/controllers/ only handle HTTP and call the model: The model's tests use a fresh SQLite file per test tests/tasks test.pas . pastel new model writes a model for a new table — its migration, the unit and its tests — from a list of fields: Type SQL Pascal string varchar 200 string text text string integer , bigint integer , bigint Integer , Int64 number double precision Double money decimal 14,2 Currency boolean integer 0/1 Boolean date , datetime text 2026 11 03 , 2026 11 03 09:30:00 string ! after the type makes the field required TCustomer.Check refuses it empty . The unit has TCustomer one row, published properties, so TDataBinding.LoadObject fills a form from it and TCustomers the table : pastel migrate makes the table; the tests run with pastel test . The generated code is yours to change. Backups Backup Restore SQLite a database file VACUUM INTO , safe while the app works the file replaces the database; nothing else may use it meanwhile PostgreSQL SQL from pg dump sudo apt install postgresql client psql ru

title: Data that works offline: Pastel.Sync
text: Data that works offline: Pastel.Sync A shop's computer, a field worker's laptop, a phone: they should keep working when the network is down, and the server should still end up with everything. Pastel.Sync does this. Every computer keeps its own SQLite file; a sync sends what changed there and takes what changed elsewhere. The salon example guide business.md is built on it. The store AddTable takes the columns as SQL, without the ones every table gets: id , updated at , synced at , dirty , deleted . The same code runs on the computers and on the server, so both check the data the same way. OnCheck runs before every Save , and for every record that comes with a sync — the other side may be an old or a broken program. Syncing The computer: FLastSync is the server's time of the last sync; keep it in the settings and give it again next time, so only newer changes come. When the server cannot be reached, SyncWithServer raises EHttpError and nothing is lost: the changes stay marked and go next time. The server: How it works Rule Why Ids are made where the record is made: 16 random characters Two computers that both add a customer offline never get the same id Every change stamps updated at UTC, with milliseconds When a record was changed on two computers, the newer change wins A computer marks what it changes dirty Only those are sent; after the server took them, they are not marked any more Nothing is really deleted: deleted = 1 A deletion travels like any change The server stamps what it stores with its own clock synced at "What is new for you" does not depend on the computers' clocks Sending the same records twice changes nothing, so a sync that broke off halfway is simply done again. When "the newer wins" is not right: for a phone number it is. For a stock count it is not — two shops that each sold one would end with one sale. There, store the change as its own record 1 shampoo , a new id each time and add them up. Without HTTP Changes , Apply and MarkSent are what SyncWithServer uses, for other ways of moving the data a file on a USB stick, a message queue :

title: Users and login: Pastel.Auth
text: Users and login: Pastel.Auth A server with users, passwords and roles, and apps that log in to it. The server Route POST /api/auth/login {"email", "password"} → {"token", "refresh token", "expires in", "user"} ; 401 when wrong; at most 10 tries a minute from one address POST /api/auth/refresh {"refresh token"} → new tokens; a refresh token works once POST /api/auth/logout {"refresh token"} → the refresh token is removed GET /api/auth/me The user of the token In a handler, the token's claims say who asks: Req.Claim 'sub' the user's id , email , name , role . Managing users: Add Email, Password, Name, Role , Check Email, Password , Find Id , FindByEmail , List , SetPassword also logs the user out everywhere , SetRole , SetActive Id, False . How it is kept safe: passwords are stored as PBKDF2 SHA256 hashes with a salt 210,000 rounds ; a wrong e mail takes as long as a wrong password, so answers do not tell which e mails exist; the token a JWT is valid for 15 minutes, the refresh token for 30 days, stored only as a hash, and replaced at every use. Put the server behind HTTPS deploy.md deploy.md . The app LoginDialog asks for the e mail and the password, and shows the last problem Client.Error : a wrong password, no network, too many tries in the app's language. Client.User is the user name , role — show or hide what their role may do. To stay logged in between starts, keep Client.RefreshToken in the user's settings and next time call Client.ResumeWith Saved ; it is False when the user must log in again. Client.Logout ends it on the server too. Login Email, Password , Logout , LoggedIn , ResumeWith RefreshToken Get Path , PostJson Path, Json , Delete Path Requests with the token User , Error , RefreshToken , Http

title: Passwords, tokens and signatures: Pastel.Crypto, Pastel.Jwt
text: Passwords, tokens and signatures: Pastel.Crypto , Pastel.Jwt What a web API or a service needs to keep secrets safe. Written in Pascal, tested against the official test vectors; no OpenSSL needed. Passwords Never store passwords, only a hash made for passwords: The hash looks like pbkdf2 sha256$210000$<salt $<hash : PBKDF2 with HMAC SHA256, 210 000 rounds and a new random salt for every password, so equal passwords give different hashes and guessing is slow about 0.4 s per try on a PC . The rounds are stored in the hash, so a later Pastel can use more without breaking old hashes. VerifyPassword compares in constant time and returns False for anything that is not such a hash. Random tokens From the system's secure source /dev/urandom , RtlGenRandom on Windows : for API keys, session ids, password reset links, secrets. Never use Random for these. Comparing secrets takes the same time whether the first or the last character differs, so an attacker cannot find a key character by character by timing the answers. JSON Web Tokens HS256 only; tokens that name another algorithm or none are refused. iat and exp are added; exp and nbf are checked, with 30 seconds of leeway for clocks. The secret should be long and random RandomToken , the same on every server, and kept in the settings or an environment variable. A JWT is signed, not encrypted: anyone can read its claims. Put nothing secret in it. In a web server, Web.RequireJwt '/api', Secret checks the tokens web.md web.md . Hashes and signatures Sha256 Data , Sha256Hex Data SHA 256 of bytes or text Sha256File FileName of a file, as hex HmacSha256 Key, Data to sign messages, e.g. webhooks Pbkdf2Sha256 Password, Salt, Rounds, Length to derive keys Base64UrlEncode , Base64UrlDecode , ToHex Checking a webhook signature, for example: Encryption: Pastel.Cipher AES 256 GCM: what is encrypted cannot be read without the key, and any change to it is found. EncryptText makes the key from the password PBKDF2 SHA256, a new salt each time ; a new nonce every time. Tested against NIST's vectors. Secrets on the device: Pastel.SecureStore Tokens and passwords an app keeps between runs, where the system keeps secrets: Android: encrypted with a key of the phone's Keystore the key never leaves its secure hardware . Windows: the user's data protection DPAPI . Linux: the desktop's keyring GNOME Keyring, KWallet through secret tool ; without a desktop session a file only the user can read ~/.config/<app /secrets . SecureStoreKind says which. What the web server and the database layer protect against Reviewed for 0.7; each point has a test in framework/tests . Threat What Pastel does SQL injection Values are always sent as parameters ? , never put into the SQL text; ? and : inside quotes stay text. Huge requests Bodies over max body mb 8 MB get 413 before anything is read or reserved; headers over 64 KB get 431. Slow clients "slowloris" A request must arrive within request timeout 30 s , and no single wait may be longer than half of it: 408. Too many connections Over max connections 256 , new connections get 503 at once instead of a thread each. Path traversal Static files are only served from inside their folder: .. , %2e%2e , %2f , \ and %00 give 404, and the final path is checked once more. Content sniffing Every answer has X Content Type Options: nosniff . Spoofed client addresses Behind a proxy trust proxy , only the last X Forwarded For address counts the one the proxy added . Rate limit bypass Limits are per client address, looked up in a sorted list, so many addresses do not slow the server down. Guessable secrets API keys and signatures are compared in constant time SameSecret ; JWTs must be HS256 no none , no algorithm switching ; passwords use PBKDF2 SHA256 with 210 000 rounds. Leaking errors Release builds answer 500 with a general message; the details go to the log. Passwords in logs TDatabase.SafeUrl leaves the password out of database addresses. Not covered by Pastel itself: HTTPS put nginx or

title: Deploying to a Linux server
text: Deploying to a Linux server Three ways, from simplest to most packaged. All of them start with a release build from pastel package ; the program is one file and needs no runtime on the server. Use it when pastel package copying a folder is enough: .tar.gz with the program and its files pastel package deb Debian, Ubuntu, Raspberry Pi OS servers: apt install , systemd, upgrades pastel package docker the server runs containers Docker, Podman, Kubernetes A .deb On the server: What goes where: /opt/myapi/ the program, README, and what package include lists migrations too /usr/lib/systemd/system/myapi.service deploy/myapi.service services /etc/myapi/config.toml config.example.toml services ; kept on upgrades when you changed it /var/lib/myapi/ the service's data the SQLite database , made by systemd /usr/bin/myapi a link to the program console programs and apps The service is enabled on install but not started, so you can set it up first; an upgrade apt install of a newer .deb restarts it if it was running. apt remove myapi stops it; the data in /var/lib stays. pastel.toml : The .deb is made by Pastel itself, so it can be made on Windows and macOS too. An API whose settings still have the example API key CHANGE ME ... does not start: it says so in the journal. A container image The image is Debian slim package.docker base = "..." for another with the packages of package.deb depends . The program runs as a user without rights, logs JSON to the container's output, listens on all addresses port 8080 and has a health check. Settings come from environment variables: MYAPI DATABASE URL=postgres://... , MYAPI API KEYS=key1,key2 , MYAPI LOG LEVEL=debug . docker stop stops it cleanly. HTTPS: a reverse proxy in front The Pastel web server speaks plain HTTP and listens on 127.0.0.1 ; a reverse proxy on the same machine adds HTTPS and the domain name. Caddy gets the certificate by itself , /etc/caddy/Caddyfile : nginx , with a certificate from certbot nginx : Then set server trust proxy = true , so client addresses logs, rate limits come from the proxy's X Forwarded For web.md web.md . With WebSockets websockets.md , their addresses also need: Checklist Real secrets in /etc/myapi/config.toml or the environment, never in the code or the image. server address = "127.0.0.1" behind a proxy; the firewall opens only 80 and 443. /health for monitoring. Backups of /var/lib/myapi SQLite: sqlite3 app.db ".backup backup.db" while it runs or of the database server. Services and systemd in detail: services.md services.md .
headings: HTTPS: a reverse proxy in front

title: The project file: pastel.toml
text: The project file: pastel.toml Every Pastel project has a pastel.toml in its main folder. pastel finds it from any sub folder, so commands work anywhere in the project. Only project name is required. Mistakes are reported with the line: pastel.toml: line 7: invalid value "yes" strings need quotes . Defines everywhere Every build also has: Define When PASTEL always PASTEL DEBUG debug and test builds PASTEL RELEASE release builds PASTEL TEST pastel test and the unit AppInfo with AppName , AppVersion , AppProfile debug , release or test and AppTarget . Debug and release builds Debug default Release release Speed not optimized optimized O2 Checks range, overflow and I/O checks, assertions off Debug information DWARF 3, readable in gdb none, smaller program .pform files read at run time hot reload built into the program Windows apps without a console window: WriteLn goes to the console that started them pastel run , cmd the same Output build/<platform /debug/ build/<platform /release/ Packages: pastel package A package is a release build in an archive: .zip for Windows, .tar.gz for the others. It contains one folder, inventory 1.2.0 linux/ , with the program executable on Linux and macOS , README , LICENSE and CHANGELOG files from the project folder, what package include and package.<platform include list: files, folders with their contents and patterns like docs/ .md , relative to the project. Next to every archive is a .sha256 file, so receivers can check it: sha256sum c inventory 1.2.0 linux.tar.gz.sha256 . For servers there are also pastel package deb a Debian/Ubuntu package with the systemd unit and pastel package docker a container image : deploy.md deploy.md . Desktop apps need SDL2 and FreeType on the computer that runs them. On Linux they come with the system sudo apt install libsdl2 2.0 0 libfreetype6 ; for Windows, put SDL2.dll and freetype.dll in the project for example libs/windows/ and list them in package.windows include . Upgrading a project pastel = "0.7" records the Pastel version a project is made for; pastel new writes it. When a newer Pastel builds an older project, the build says so, and brings the project up to date: it sets pastel , renames things that newer versions treat differently for example a control named Hint , which hides the Hint property since 0.5 , adds a title to apps and keeps build/ and dist/ out of git. Projects made for a newer Pastel than the one installed get a warning: update pastel . From 1.0 on, pastel.toml , .pform files and the public framework API stay compatible within 1.x: what builds with 1.0 builds with every 1.x.

title: Everyday work: watch, format, libraries
text: Everyday work: watch, format, libraries pastel run watch Build and run again every time you save pastel test watch Run the tests again every time you save pastel fmt Format the code in one standard style pastel new lib A library: units that other projects use dependencies Use another Pastel project or a package from this one packages.md packages.md Watch: pastel run watch Every Pascal file of the project is watched, and the units of its dependencies, and pastel.toml . A program that is still running when you save is asked to stop SIGTERM, so it can clean up; after 3 seconds it is stopped and started again with the new code. That makes it handy for servers too. After a compile error Pastel waits: fix the code, save, and it continues. Arguments for your program go after : pastel run watch port 9000 . In a desktop app, .pform changes appear in the running window by themselves hot reload ; only code changes restart the app. pastel test watch does the same for the tests, also when a test file changes. With a filter it runs only some of them: pastel test watch greeting . In VS Code: Pastel: Run and Watch and Pastel: Test and Watch in the command palette, or the pastel: watch task in new projects. Format: pastel fmt What it does: indentation from the structure of the code: two spaces per level; begin lines up with its if , for or while ; else with its if ; except and finally with their try ; members of a class one level in, private / public at the level of the class; case labels one level in, their statements one more reserved words in lower case: BEGIN → begin , String → string a space around := and after , ; none before , and ; trailing spaces, more than one empty line in a row, tabs at the start of a line What it leaves alone: line breaks: it never joins or splits lines comments and strings; asm blocks the shape of a statement that continues on the next line it moves as a whole extra spaces used to line things up: X := 1; anything between // fmt: off and // fmt: on It is careful: a file whose begin / end do not match is reported and not changed src/x.pas: line 40: "begin" from line 12 has no matching "end" , and after formatting the code is read back and compared with the original; if anything but spacing would change, nothing is written. Settings, in pastel.toml : In VS Code, Format Document Shift+Alt+F uses pastel fmt , and new projects format on save "editor.formatOnSave" in .vscode/settings.json . Code that cannot be formatted while you type is left as it is, with a note in the status bar. Libraries: pastel new lib creates A library has no program of its own: pastel build compiles every unit in src/ to find mistakes pastel test runs its tests pastel run explains that there is nothing to run Dependencies To use the library from another project, add it to that project's pastel.toml : and use its units as usual: The path is relative to the project an absolute path works too . The dependency's src/ folders and its build unit paths are added to the search path. Its tests are not. A dependency's own dependencies are added too; each project once, even if several need it. Changes in a dependency are compiled with your project, and watch sees them. Any Pastel project can be a dependency, not only libraries; usually it is a library. Packages from the internet — from the registry or a git repository, with versions and pastel.lock — are explained in packages.md packages.md . A group of projects: pastel new group Programs that belong together — a server, a desktop app, a phone app and the library they share — are kept side by side in one folder, and a pastel.toml with group in that folder makes them a group, like Delphi's project group: pastel new group in that folder writes it: the folders with a pastel.toml , libraries before the projects that use them, run the first app. In the group's folder: In a project's own folder the commands are that project's, as always. Other commands add , migrate , package ... are run in a project
headings: A group of projects: pastel new group

title: Packages
text: Packages A package is a Pastel library that someone published: serial ports, charts, a barcode reader. You add it with one command, and Pastel fetches it, keeps its exact version in pastel.lock and compiles it with your project. It works like Composer for PHP or npm for JavaScript. Composer PHP Pastel composer.json → require pastel.toml → dependencies composer.lock pastel.lock composer require x pastel add x composer update pastel update composer install nothing to do: pastel build fetches what is missing composer remove x pastel remove x Packagist the registry: github.com/azrov/pastel packages https://github.com/azrov/pastel packages vendor/ one cache for all projects: ~/.cache/pastel Free Pascal's own packages Free Pascal comes with about 140 packages, and a Pastel project can use all of them without adding anything: write the unit in uses and build. Pastel itself is built on several fpjson , fphttpclient , sqldb , process . Some useful ones: Package Units For paszlib zipper , zstream Zip files, compressed streams regexpr RegExpr Regular expressions hash md5 , sha1 , crc Checksums fcl base base64 , IniFiles , CustApp , uriparser Everyday helpers fcl xml DOM , XMLRead , XMLWrite , XPath XML fcl image fpimage , fpreadpng , fpwritejpeg ... Reading and writing pictures rtl generics , fcl stl Generics.Collections , gmap , ghashmap Lists and dictionaries of any type fcl db sqldb , sqlite3conn , pqconnection , mysql80conn Databases directly Pastel.Db is easier fcl net , fcl web ssockets , fphttpclient , fphttpserver Network Pastel.Http and Pastel.Web are easier numlib , symbolic typ , inv , symbolic Mathematics Packages that wrap a C library libcurl , openssl , sdl , cairo , gtk2 , libvlc ... also need that library on the computer the program runs on. Building for another system pastel build target win64 needs Free Pascal's packages for that system too; pastel doctor install win64 sets them up. Adding a package pastel.toml gets a line: and the code uses its units like your own: A library's controls and components appear in the designer's toolbox, like the project's own components.md components.md . From a git repository A package that is not in the registry your company's own, or one being written comes straight from its repository: git The repository: https://... , git@... with your SSH key: private repositories work , or a folder path The folder of the package in the repository, when it holds several version A range of its tags below branch The newest commit of a branch instead of a version; pastel update moves to the newest again rev One commit From a folder on this computer Nothing is fetched or locked: the folder is used as it is, and changes in it are compiled right away workflow.md workflow.md dependencies . Versions A package's versions are the tags of its repository: v1.2.3 or 1.2.3 . In pastel.toml you write which versions are fine — usually with ^ , which allows everything that should not break your code: Written Allows "^1.2.0" = 1.2.0 , < 2.0.0 the default of pastel add "^0.3.1" = 0.3.1 , < 0.4.0 before 1.0, the second number counts "~1.2.3" = 1.2.3 , < 1.3.0 only fixes "1.2.3" exactly 1.2.3 "1.2" any 1.2.x " =1.0, <1.5" a range " " any version Pre releases 1.0.0 rc.1 are only used when the range names one: "^1.0.0 rc.1" . pastel.lock pastel add and pastel update write pastel.lock next to pastel.toml : the exact version and commit of every package, also of the packages your packages use. Put it in git. Every computer — yours, a colleague's, the CI — then builds with exactly the same code, until someone runs pastel update . pastel build never changes a locked version; it only adds what is new in pastel.toml . When two libraries need versions of a package that cannot both be met one ^1.0 , the other ^2.0 , Pastel says so and changes nothing; update one of them. Where packages are kept Each repository is fetched once and each version is unpacked once, into a cache for all projects: Linux ~/.cache/pastel or $XDG

title: Testing
text: Testing Tests live in the tests/ folder of a project. Run them with: pastel test builds every unit in tests/ into one test program, together with your project's own units, and runs it. The exit code is 1 when a test fails, so it works in CI as is. In VS Code: Pastel: Run Tests , or Run Tests in the Pastel panel. Writing tests A test file is a unit. Each published method of a TTestSuite class is one test: Method names become readable test names: GreetsByName is shown as "greets by name", and the suite TGreetingTests as "Greeting". A failing assert shows the file and line of the test. An unexpected exception is reported as an error with its class, message and line. Set up and tear down Override SetUp and TearDown to prepare and clean up for every test. Each test gets a fresh suite object, so fields start empty in every test. Tests without a class For a quick check, a plain procedure works too: Asserts Assert Passes when AssertTrue Cond / AssertFalse Cond the condition is true / false AssertEquals Expected, Actual equal; for text, whole numbers, booleans and floating point numbers with an optional Delta AssertNotEquals NotExpected, Actual different text, whole numbers AssertContains Part, Actual Actual contains Part AssertStartsWith Prefix, Actual Actual starts with Prefix AssertNil P / AssertNotNil P the pointer or object is / is not nil AssertRaises EClass, @Proc calling Proc raises EClass or a descendant ; Proc can be a method of the suite Fail Msg never: fails with a message Skip Reason never: marks the test as skipped Every assert takes an optional last argument with your own message, shown next to the failure. Good to know Tests are compiled in debug mode with range and overflow checks, so mistakes like reading past the end of an array show up as errors. The define PASTEL TEST is set while compiling tests: {$IFDEF PASTEL TEST} ... {$ENDIF} . The test program is built in build/<platform /test/ ; you never need to touch it. In VS Code With the Pastel extension, the Testing view the flask icon lists every test of the project: files, suites and tests, read from tests/ as you type. Click ▶ next to a test, a suite, a file or the whole project to run it; a failed test shows its message at the line of the failing assert. The debug icon runs the chosen tests in the debugger, so a breakpoint in the test or in the code it tests stops there. Behind the scenes this is pastel test json , with exact names to run single tests:

title: Pastel for Visual Studio Code
text: Pastel for Visual Studio Code Build cross platform apps in Object Pascal with Pastel. This extension connects VS Code to the pastel command line tool. Requirements The pastel program on your PATH or set pastel.path . Check your setup with Pastel: Check Setup . Free Pascal https://www.freepascal.org/ 3.2 or newer. Recommended: C/C++ ms vscode.cpptools for debugging with F5. Features Run and build. Press the Pastel Run button in the status bar, or use the commands Pastel: Run , Build , Build Release , Build for Platform… and Clean . Ctrl+Shift+B builds. Run F9 starts the program of the open file; when that file belongs to a library, it runs a program that uses the library with several, it asks once; Pastel: Choose the Program to Run asks again , or offers the library's tests. A folder with a group of projects a pastel.toml with group , like Delphi's project group; Pastel: New Group of Projects shows them in the side bar: F9, Ctrl+F9 and the platform are for the active project click another one, or Pastel: Set Active Project , and Build All , Build All Platforms and Test All go through every project. Errors from your Pascal code and from .pform files appear in the Problems panel; click one to jump to the line. Platform. Next to Pastel Run the status bar shows the platform F9 and Ctrl+F9 use, like Delphi's target platforms: this computer, or android for a phone app. Click it or Pastel: Choose Platform… to choose another: with android , F9 builds for the connected phone's or emulator's CPU, installs the app and shows its log, and Ctrl+F9 makes the .apk ; with android arm older phones, TV boxes or android x86 64 the emulator only that kind is built. A Windows program chosen on Linux is built, not run. See Android ../docs/android.md in vs code . Pastel: Android Log shows the log of the app on the connected phone, with the Pascal line of a crash. Views. The box at the top left of the designer chooses All screens or a view for phones, tablets, TVs or desktops Home.tablet.pform : with a view chosen, what you change goes into the view's file. See Forms ../docs/forms.md views a form for each kind of screen . App icon. Pastel: Set App Icon… also in the Pastel side bar, and on a .png in the Explorer makes a PNG the app's icon, assets/icon.png : the window, the .exe , installers and the phone's home screen. Form designer. Open a .pform file and press the designer button in the editor title. The form is drawn beside the editor and updates as you type. Click a control to select it and edit its properties; drag controls to move them; drag new ones in from the toolbox; press Delete to remove one. Ctrl+C / X / V / D copy, cut, paste and duplicate controls, F2 renames one its uses in the .pas code too , Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo and redo. Show the form at other sizes or in the dark theme from the designer's toolbar. Selection follows the cursor in the editor and the other way round. Pastel: New Form… adds a dialog form to the project. Ctrl+click or Shift+click selects several controls: the properties they all have are edited at once; delete, copy and cut work on all of them. ⊞ Row , ⊞ Column , ⊞ Card put the selected controls into a new container; Unwrap takes them out again. Alt+Up / Down or ↑ ↓ moves a control earlier or later; Escape selects its container. Structure lists every object of the form, also timers, actions and other components that are not drawn; click one to select it. What pastel check finds a row whose controls do not fit, an unknown property is outlined on the form and listed under it; click to select the control. Writing forms. title: Compatibility: what stays the same
text: Compatibility: what stays the same Pastel is heading for 1.0. From 1.0 on, a project that builds with Pastel 1.0 builds with every 1.x version. Before 1.0, changes are still possible, but they are made on purpose, listed in the changelog, and pastel upgrade carries projects along where it can. What is covered Stays compatible Checked by Framework API Every public declaration in docs/api/stable.txt api/stable.txt : units, types, routines, methods, properties, constants. New things may be added; nothing listed is removed or changed. tests/run.sh fails when a line of stable.txt is gone pastel.toml The keys in project.md project.md . Unknown keys are reported, never silently ignored. The project file tests .pform files The syntax in forms.md forms.md the pform format and the published properties of the controls they are part of the API above . The .pform reader tests pastel commands Commands and options in pastel help ; exit codes: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 wrong usage. json output only gets new fields. The end to end tests assets/ icon.png , font.ttf , font bold.ttf , theme.toml , lang/ .json The end to end tests What is not covered Declarations whose comment starts with Internal and the units marked Internal unit Pastel.Forms , Pastel.PForm , Pastel.NativeDialogs , and the platform units Pastel.SDL2 , Pastel.FreeType , Pastel.Startup , Pastel.ErrorExit . They exist for Pastel itself and the code it generates. They are left out of the API reference. The code Pastel generates build/.../gen/ . How things look: the default colors, sizes and fonts of the controls may improve. Set the look you depend on in assets/theme.toml . Messages of the pastel tool meant for people not json . For Pastel's developers Run freeze only when a change to the stable API is meant before 1.0, or for a new major version . Mark helpers that must be public for technical reasons with an { Internal: ... } comment. A project records the Pastel version it is made for in pastel.toml pastel = "0.7" ; see Upgrading a project project.md upgrading a project .

title: Performance
text: Performance sh tests/perf.sh measures what a Pastel program costs: start up time, size, memory, requests per second and drawing speed. CI runs it on every change and fails when a number is far beyond its limit the limits are generous: they catch mistakes, not small changes . The programs are release builds of the examples. Measured on a small cloud machine 2 CPUs, x86 64 for 0.7: What Measured Limit Console program: start and exit 1 ms < 100 ms Desktop app: start, first frame, exit no screen 27 ms < 500 ms Console program size 388 KB < 3 MB Desktop app size notepad ; SDL2 and FreeType are shared libraries 900 KB < 8 MB Desktop app memory 8 MB < 80 MB Web service memory, idle notes api 3 MB < 40 MB Requests per second GET /health , a new connection for each 2 681 1 000 Failed requests under that load 0 0 Web service memory after the load 3 MB < 80 MB Drawing a whole 1024×768 window with 30 controls and a 10 000 row grid 74 frames/s 25 Drawing one changed control a blinking caret, a hovered button 1 212 frames/s 200 What makes it fast Programs are native code compiled by Free Pascal: no runtime to start, no garbage collector. Only what changed is drawn. A control that changes asks for its own area to be painted again; the window is drawn completely only after a layout change. PASTEL CHECK REPAINT=1 compares every partial repaint with a full one the UI tests run with it ; PASTEL FULL REPAINT=1 turns partial repaints off. Long lists draw only the visible rows TListBox , TGrid , TListView , TTreeView . The web server handles every connection in its own thread and keeps no per request state beyond the request. What is slower than it could be The web server opens a new connection for every request no keep alive in FPC 3.2.2's server ; behind nginx or Caddy this does not matter, since the proxy keeps the connections to the clients. Drawing is done by the CPU. A GPU backend Skia is planned after 1.0 for apps with heavy graphics.

title: contacts
text: contacts A desktop address book: a list with search on the left, the contact on the right, menus and shortcuts, a confirmation before deleting. title: dupfinder
text: dupfinder Finds files with the same content. An example of a Pastel console tool; see docs/guide cli.md for how it was built. It compares sizes first, and reads only files that have the same size as another file. Nothing is deleted: it only reports.

title: notepad

title: salon-api
text: salon api The server of the salon system salon core ../salon core : it keeps the data of every computer in the shop and answers their synchronization; a small read only API shows the data to other programs a web page, a phone app . Route POST /api/sync {"since": "...", "changes": {...}} from the desktop: takes its changes, answers with what changed since its last sync GET /api/customers?q=ayşe Customers whose name, phone or e mail contain q GET /api/appointments?date=2026 11 03 The appointments of a day, with the customer's name GET /api/invoices The invoices, newest first GET /api/invoices/:id/pdf One invoice as PDF the same as the desktop's, from SalonPrint ../salon core/src/salonprint.pas GET /api/invoices.xlsx Every invoice as an Excel file, to download GET /health For monitoring Settings are in config.toml database url for PostgreSQL or MySQL; salon address , the name and address on invoices; api keys so only the shop's computers get in . See docs/web.md ../../docs/web.md and docs/deploy.md ../../docs/deploy.md .

title: salon-core
text: salon core The shared part of a small business system — a hair salon here, but the same fits a clinic, a repair shop or a tutor: customers, appointments and invoices , and the synchronization between the computers in the shop and the server. It is a library type = "lib" used by two programs: salon desk ../salon desk The desktop app in the shop Linux, Windows . Works without a network, on a SQLite file; a click on Sync exchanges the changes with the server salon api ../salon api The server: keeps everything PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite and answers POST /api/sync ; also a small read only API Both use the same units, so a customer is checked and stored the same way on the desktop and on the server. Unit SalonStore The tables, saving with checks, lists, a day's appointments, invoices with VAT, and the sync: Changes , Apply , MarkSent — on Pastel.Sync ../../docs/sync.md SalonSync The desktop side of the sync over HTTP SalonMoney Money in cents: CentsToText , TryTextToCents , VatOf SalonPrint An invoice as PDF or HTML InvoiceReport , Pastel.Report ../../docs/documents.md , the invoices as an Excel file InvoicesSheet How the sync works: every record gets its id where it is made no clashes between computers and updated at , the time of its last change. The desktop marks what it changes dirty , sends it, and takes what the server got from the other computers since its last sync. When both sides changed a record, the newer change wins. Records are never deleted, only marked, so deletions travel too.

title: salon-desk
text: salon desk The desktop app of the salon system: the computer at the reception of a hair salon or a clinic, a repair shop... . It uses salon core ../salon core for the data and the invoices' PDF, and components ../components for remembering the settings. ! The salon app in Turkish: a day of appointments ../../docs/images/salon.png Page Appointments One day ‹ › Today, or the date picker : the appointments with time, customer, service, price and status; a form to add or change one; Done and Cancel Customers Search, the list, and the customer's details a TDataBinding Invoices Invoices of the done appointments of a customer, with VAT; Mark as paid ; PDF saved next to the database and opened , Print , Excel all invoices as .xlsx The data is a SQLite file in the user's settings folder SALON DB=file.db for another one , so the app works without a network. File Sync Ctrl+R exchanges the changes with the server salon api ../salon api ; its address and API key, the VAT and the salon's name and address for invoices are in File Settings . The app is in English and Turkish assets/lang/tr.json ; PASTEL LANG=tr to try it . The tests drive the app without a screen: tests/sync.txt and tests/sync 2.txt are two computers syncing through a running salon api see tests/run.sh . How the whole system is built: docs/guide business.md ../../docs/guide business.md .

title: Pastel roadmap to 1.0
text: Pastel roadmap to 1.0 Pastel grows in this order: console programs → Linux services → desktop apps . Each step builds on the one before: a service is a console program that runs for a long time, and a desktop app uses the same libraries as a service. Every milestone ends with something you can really use, and with tests and documentation for it. Items are checked off as they are done. Version 1.0 means: you can build and ship a real console tool, a real Linux service REST API with a database, packaged and running under systemd and a real desktop business app Linux and Windows with Pastel, using VS Code, without hitting a wall. File formats pastel.toml , .pform and public APIs are stable from 1.0 on. 0.1 — Foundation done What exists today. Tool pastel x new console , new app , build , run , clean , targets , doctor x Debug and release builds, compiler errors with file and line x Cross compiling to Windows and Raspberry Pi when the cross compilers are installed x check , preview , schema for editors GUI framework x Window, event loop, software rendering with FreeType text SDL2 x .pform forms, generated base classes, RTTI properties and events x Controls: label, button, edit, card, row, column, spacer x Flexbox style layout, keyboard focus, clipboard x Window settings and events resizable, maximize, close query, ... x Hot reload of .pform files, headless mode and UI test scripts VS Code extension x Run/Build commands and Delphi keys, problems panel x Form designer select, properties, drag and drop, toolbox x .pform completion, checks, quick fixes x Pascal colors, outline, go to definition, symbol search x Pastel panel in the activity bar 0.2 — Console programs, complete done Goal: writing a command line tool in Pastel is pleasant from the first line to the release. Tool x pastel test : finds and runs tests in tests/ , clear report, exit code for CI x pastel run watch : rebuild and restart when a file changes also pastel test watch x pastel fmt : format Pascal code with one standard style check for CI, stdin for editors x pastel package : a .tar.gz Linux or .zip Windows with the program, ready to hand out x pastel new lib : a library project that other projects can use x Use another local Pastel project as a dependency dependencies in pastel.toml x pastel.toml : version shown by the program version , generated AppInfo unit x pastel.toml : build time defines per profile Library Pastel.Core , usable without the GUI x Pastel.Testing : test cases, asserts with readable messages x Pastel.Args : command line arguments and sub commands, automatic help x Pastel.Term : colors, tables, progress bars, prompts yes/no, input, choice x Pastel.Text : upper/lower case and lengths for every language Turkish/Azerbaijani i x UTF 8 everywhere, also in the Windows console; thread support without cthreads in uses x Pastel.Log : log levels, to the console or a file, with timestamps also JSON, journald, rotation, threads x Pastel.Config : settings from .toml , .json and environment variables x Pastel.Json : easy reading and writing of JSON on top of FPC's fpjson x Pastel.Files and Pastel.Process : paths, reading/writing files, running other programs x Pastel.Http client: GET/POST with JSON, timeouts, HTTPS with certificate checks, proxies x Pastel.Env : environment variables in UTF 8 also on Windows VS Code x Test explorer: run and debug single tests from the editor x Pascal snippets class, procedure, try/finally, for, case, ... x F5 debugging without manual setup; readable strings and arrays in the debugger x Format on save uses pastel fmt Docs x Getting started guide install, first project, debug, release : docs/getting started.md x Console programs: docs/console.md ; testing: docs/testing.md ; JSON, settings, logging: docs/data.md ; files, programs, HTTP: docs/system.md ; watch, format, libraries: docs/workflow.md ; pastel.toml and packages: docs/project.md x Guide: writing a command line tool: docs/guide cli.md x Examples: a file tool, a too

title: Contributing to Pastel
text: Contributing to Pastel Thank you for helping! Pastel is a Delphi like way to build console programs, services and desktop apps in Object Pascal, with VS Code and Free Pascal. Bug reports, ideas, documentation fixes and code are all welcome. Asking and reporting A bug: open an issue with the Bug form. The output of pastel version and pastel doctor , and the smallest project that shows the problem, help most. An idea: open an issue with the Idea form and describe what you want to build, not only the feature. ROADMAP.md ROADMAP.md shows what is planned. A security problem: do not open an issue; see SECURITY.md SECURITY.md . Getting the code running You need Free Pascal 3.2.2 sudo apt install fpc fpc source , Node.js 20 for the VS Code extension, and for the desktop tests SDL2 and FreeType sudo apt install libsdl2 2.0 0 libfreetype6 . The database tests also run against PostgreSQL and MySQL/MariaDB when PASTEL TEST POSTGRES URL and PASTEL TEST MYSQL URL are set see .github/workflows/ci.yml . The Android end to end tests run when ppcrossa64 and the ARM 64 bit binutils are there, the .apk ones with aapt , zipalign , apksigner and android sdk platform 23 see docs/android.md docs/android.md . Windows programs are tested too when Wine is installed sudo apt install wine64 : the salon example is built for Windows and its screens, database and sync run under Wine. The VS Code extension has its own tests: npm test and npm run test:integration <a new app project in vscode/ . How the repository is organized Folder What is in it cli/ The pastel tool: commands, builder, code generation for forms, packaging framework/src/ The units programs use Pastel. ; framework/tests/ tests them framework/android/ Pastel's small Java activity for Android and its classes.dex rebuilt with tools/android dex.sh when the Java changes vscode/ The VS Code extension: designer, Pascal code intelligence, tasks examples/ Complete programs; each has tests and is built in CI docs/ The guides and the API reference docs/api is generated tests/ Unit tests of the tool, run.sh end to end , perf.sh performance tools/ The website tools/website , a Pastel program , the release scripts, android dex.sh Pastel's Android activity and android sqlite.sh SQLite for Android apps, kept in framework/android/lib/ Making a change 1. Discuss bigger changes first in an issue, so no work is lost. 2. Write a test for what you fix or add: a framework test framework/tests/tests/ , an end to end check tests/run.sh or a UI script see docs/forms.md docs/forms.md testing a form without a window . 3. Keep the style: bin/pastel fmt cli framework tests examples formats the Pascal code; the tests check it. 4. Document it, with an example, in the same change. Pastel's docs are meant to answer every "how do I...?" with something to copy: a comment above every public declaration it becomes the API reference: npm run apidoc in vscode/ ; a new control or component: a section TName in docs/controls.md docs/controls.md with a .pform and a code example; a new command or option: docs/commands.md docs/commands.md ; a new feature: a section in the topic's page docs/README.md docs/README.md lists them , and in the guide when it changes how a program is built; a new example program: a README.md and a line in docs/README.md docs/README.md examples ; a line in CHANGELOG.md CHANGELOG.md . tests/docs coverage.sh fails when a control, a command or an example has no documentation, and the website tools/website fails on broken links and anchors. 5. Keep compatibility: from 1.0 on, nothing in docs/api/stable.txt may be removed or changed in 1.x; add new things instead. See docs/compatibility.md docs/compatibility.md . 6. Run sh build.sh test and open a pull request. Writing style Pastel's documentation, messages and comments use plain, short English that non native speakers read easily: active sentences, common words, an example before an explanation. Error messages say what went wrong and what to do hint: ... . License By c

title: Security
text: Security Reporting a problem Please report security problems privately, through GitHub's Report a vulnerability button on the Security tab of the repository, not in a public issue. Tell us what is affected, how to reproduce it and what an attacker could do. We answer within a week and publish a fixed version as soon as possible; you are credited in the release notes unless you prefer not to be. Supported versions Version Security fixes 1.x latest yes older than 1.0 no: please upgrade pastel upgrade helps What Pastel protects against The web server and database layer were reviewed for 0.7; what they protect against and what is left to the network in front of them is in docs/security.md docs/security.md what the web server and the database layer protect against .

title: Code of conduct
text: Code of conduct Pastel follows the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1 https://www.contributor covenant.org/version/2/1/code of conduct/ . In short: be kind and patient, especially with people who are new to Pascal or to programming; criticize ideas, not people; no harassment of any kind. Many people here write in their second or third language, so read generously. Problems can be reported privately to the maintainers through the contact on the repository's profile. Reports are handled confidentially.

title: Announcing Pastel 1.0
text: Announcing Pastel 1.0 The release announcement blog, forums, Free Pascal and Lazarus communities, Hacker News . Pastel 1.0 is out: a free, Delphi like way to build programs in Object Pascal, with VS Code and Free Pascal. Many of us learned programming with Delphi: draw a form, double click a button, write the code, press F9. Pastel brings that way of working to today's tools — and to more than desktop apps. What you can build Desktop apps for Linux and Windows. Forms live in readable .pform files that you design in VS Code: drag controls in, set properties, double click an event to write its code. About 40 controls grids, trees, menus, dialogs, tabs, date pickers, money fields, tool bars, splitters, 38 icons... , data binding, translations, themes and dark mode, sharp on high DPI screens. Save the form while the app runs and the window updates at once. Web APIs and Linux services. Routes, JSON, validation, API keys and JWT, rate limits, SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL with migrations, background jobs, systemd, .deb and Docker packages. Command line tools. Arguments with automatic help, colors and tables, settings, logging, HTTP, tests. ! The contacts example images/contacts.png What it feels like VS Code knows your code and the framework: completion, hover, go to definition, rename, compiler errors while you type, a test explorer, F5 debugging with readable objects, lists and JSON. Libraries are shared like with Composer or npm: pastel add serial fetches a package, keeps its exact version in pastel.lock , and its controls appear in the designer's toolbox. The registry is pastel packages https://github.com/azrov/pastel packages ; pastel extras https://github.com/azrov/pastel extras has the first ones serial ports . When the app is ready: pastel package installer target windows makes a Windows installer, pastel package appimage and pastel package deb Linux packages — all from one Linux machine. Fast and small A console program starts in a millisecond; a desktop app is under a megabyte and draws its first frame in 30 ms; a web service uses a few megabytes of memory and answers thousands of requests per second. Pastel programs are native code compiled by Free Pascal https://www.freepascal.org/ . Stable 1.0 means the framework API, the project file, the form format and the commands stay compatible for all of 1.x. Projects from earlier versions come along with pastel upgrade . Get it Linux: curl fsSL https://github.com/azrov/pastel/releases/latest/download/install.sh sh Windows: the .zip from the release page VS Code: the .vsix from the release page Extensions → ⋯ → Install from VSIX Docs and guides: github.com/azrov/pastel/tree/main/docs https://github.com/azrov/pastel/tree/main/docs ; start with Getting started Pastel is MIT licensed and made in the open. Bug reports, ideas and contributions are very welcome — see CONTRIBUTING.md https://github.com/azrov/pastel/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md .

title: Pastel.Accessibility
text: Pastel.Accessibility Screen readers: what is on the screen, for people who cannot see it. Pastel draws its controls itself, so it tells the system what they are: on Android TalkBack reads each control its kind, its text, checked or not , and a double tap clicks it nothing to do in the app. A control whose text does not say what it does gets an AccessibleName: object DeleteButton: TButton Icon = 'trash' AccessibleName = 'Delete the appointment' end Computers: Windows' Narrator and Linux's Orca are not reached yet. uses Pastel.Accessibility; · source: framework/src/pastel.accessibility.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.accessibility.pas Other types type TPixelRectFunc = function R: TRectI : TRectI Routines AccessibilityTree The controls a screen reader sees, a line each: id, parent's id, x, y, w, h pixels , role Android's class , text, hint, flags. title: Pastel.Android
text: Pastel.Android The bridge to Android: an app is a NativeActivity, so it needs no Java code. Android calls ANativeActivity onCreate exported by the app's libmain.so ; Pastel then runs the app on a thread of its own, which gets the window, the touches and the keys from here. The calls from Android window made, app paused, input... arrive on Android's main thread; they are passed to the app thread through a pipe, and the ones that change the window or the input queue wait until the app thread has taken them like android native app glue of the NDK, written in Pascal . uses Pastel.Android; · source: framework/src/pastel.android.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.android.pas

title: Pastel.Auth
text: Pastel.Auth Users, passwords and roles for a server, and login for its apps. The server: Users := TUserStore.Create Db ; Users.CreateTables; if Users.Count = 0 then Users.Add 'admin@shop.com', 'change me now', 'Admin', 'admin' ; AddAuthRoutes Web, Users, Secret ; // POST /api/auth/login, /refresh, /logout; GET /api/auth/me Web.RequireJwt '/api/shop', Secret ; // these routes need a login ... procedure TShop.DeleteCustomer Req: TWebRequest; Res: TWebResponse ; begin RequireRole Req, 'admin' ; // 403 for the others ... The app desktop, console : Client := TAuthClient.Create 'https://shop.example.com' ; if not Client.Login 'ayse@shop.com', Password then ShowMessage Client.Error ; R := Client.Get '/api/shop/customers' ; // with the token; a new one when it ran out Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes Pastel.Crypto . title: Pastel.Background
text: Pastel.Background Work that goes on when the app is not on the screen. Background work: the app keeps running, with a notification, while it does something the user started plays music, records a route, uploads photos . Its Pascal code goes on as before: timers, threads, the network. StartBackgroundWork 'Uploading photos', '3 of 20', bkDataSync ; UpdateBackgroundWork '7 of 20' ; StopBackgroundWork; Background jobs: a function Android runs from time to time also when the app is closed, and after the phone restarted sync, reminders, a backup . It is registered in a unit's initialization, runs on a thread of its own without the app's window no forms: data, files, HTTP and answers True when it was done False: again later . function SyncNow: Boolean; begin Result := Store.Sync ServerUrl ; end; initialization RegisterBackgroundJob 'sync', @SyncNow ; ... ScheduleBackgroundJob 'sync', 60 ; // about every hour, when there is a network pastel.toml says what the app does in the background: package.android background = "data sync" media playback, location, connected device On computers apps run as long as they are open: background work does nothing, scheduled jobs run with a timer while the app is open. uses Pastel.Background; · source: framework/src/pastel.background.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.background.pas Contents: TBackgroundKind tbackgroundkind · StartBackgroundWork startbackgroundwork · UpdateBackgroundWork updatebackgroundwork · StopBackgroundWork stopbackgroundwork · BackgroundWorkRunning backgroundworkrunning · RegisterBackgroundJob registerbackgroundjob · ScheduleBackgroundJob schedulebackgroundjob · CancelBackgroundJob cancelbackgroundjob · RunBackgroundJob runbackgroundjob · InBackgroundJob inbackgroundjob Types TBackgroundKind bkDataSync bkMediaPlayback bkLocation bkConnectedDevice Other types type TBackgroundJob = function: Boolean a background job: True when done, False when it should be tried again later Routines StartBackgroundWork The app keeps running with a notification Title, Text until StopBackgroundWork. Kind must be in pastel.toml's package.android background. UpdateBackgroundWork A new text for its notification. StopBackgroundWork BackgroundWorkRunning RegisterBackgroundJob A job by name; in a unit's initialization, so it is there when Android starts the app for it. ScheduleBackgroundJob Runs it about every EveryMinutes 15 at least , when there is a network if NeedsNetwork; also after the phone restarted. False when it could not be planned. CancelBackgroundJob RunBackgroundJob Runs a registered job now tests, a "Sync now" button ; its answer. InBackgroundJob True inside a job Android started without the app's window.

text: Pastel.Binding Data binding: fills a form's controls from a record and back. object PersonData: TDataBinding Fields = 'NameEdit', 'EmailEdit', 'ActiveCheck', 'AgeSlider=age years' end PersonData.Load Db.QueryOne 'select from people where id = ?', Id ; ... Row := TJSONObject.Create; PersonData.Save Row ; // name, email, active, age years if PersonData.Modified then ... Rules check the values before they are saved: object PersonData: TDataBinding Fields = 'NameEdit', 'EmailEdit', 'AgeEdit' Rules = 'NameEdit=required', 'EmailEdit=email', 'AgeEdit=number, range 0..120' ErrorLabel = ProblemLabel end if not PersonData.Validate then Exit; // the first wrong control is focused 'NameEdit' alone binds the field 'name' the name without the control's kind, in snake case: FullNameEdit full name . title: Pastel.Cipher
text: Pastel.Cipher Encryption: AES 256 GCM, and text sealed with a password. Sealed := EncryptText Password, 'IBAN TR12 0006 ...' ; // 'v1.' + base64url Plain := DecryptText Password, Sealed ; // ECipherError: wrong password or changed Data := AesGcmEncrypt Key, Bytes ; // Key: 32 bytes RandomBytes 32 Bytes := AesGcmDecrypt Key, Data ; AES 256 in GCM mode NIST SP 800 38D : a new random nonce every time, a tag that finds any change. EncryptText makes the key from the password with PBKDF2 SHA256 and a random salt. All in Pascal, no OpenSSL. uses Pastel.Cipher; · source: framework/src/pastel.cipher.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.cipher.pas Contents: ECipherError eciphererror · AesGcmEncrypt aesgcmencrypt · AesGcmDecrypt aesgcmdecrypt · AesGcmSeal aesgcmseal · AesGcmOpen aesgcmopen · EncryptText encrypttext · DecryptText decrypttext Types ECipherError Routines AesGcmEncrypt Key: 32 bytes. The answer: a 12 byte nonce, the cipher text, a 16 byte tag. Aad: data that is checked not encrypted with it. AesGcmDecrypt ECipherError when the key is wrong or the data was changed AesGcmSeal The same with the nonce given tests, protocols that set it : no nonce in the answer. AesGcmOpen EncryptText Text sealed with a password: 'v1.' and base64url salt, nonce, text, tag . DecryptText

title: Pastel.Config
text: Pastel.Config Settings from files, environment variables and code. Config := TConfig.Create 'myapp' ; Config.SetDefault 'server.port', '8080' ; Config.LoadStandard; // see below Port := Config.GetInt 'server.port' ; Host := Config.Get 'database.host', 'localhost' ; Pass := Config.Require 'database.password' ; // clear error if missing A setting can come from several places; the later one wins: 1. SetDefault in code 2. /etc/myapp/config.toml Linux; on Windows %ProgramData%\myapp 3. ~/.config/myapp/config.toml the user's own settings 4. ./config.toml next to where the program runs 5. environment: MYAPP SERVER PORT for server.port 6. Config.SetValue in code, e.g. from a command line option LoadStandard loads 2 5; LoadFile and LoadEnv do it step by step. Files can be TOML or JSON. title: Pastel.CrashReport
text: Pastel.CrashReport Crash reports: what went wrong on users' machines, sent to you. EnableCrashReports 'https://api.example.com/crashes', '1.4.2' ; ... try Sync; except on E: Exception do ReportError E, 'sync' ; // a caught error worth knowing about end; An exception nobody caught is written into a file before the program ends with the place it happened, the version, the system ; the next start sends the waiting reports as JSON POST, on a thread of its own and removes them. title: Pastel.Crypto
text: Pastel.Crypto Hashes, signatures, passwords and random tokens. Sha256Hex 'abc' // 'ba7816bf...' Sig := HmacSha256 Secret, Message ; // raw bytes Token := RandomToken; // 43 characters, safe in URLs Hash := HashPassword 's3cret' ; // store this, never the password if VerifyPassword Typed, Hash then ... if SameSecret Given, Expected then ... // takes the same time either way All in Pascal, no OpenSSL needed.
