title: Pastel.Db
text: Pastel.Db Databases: SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB. Db := TDatabase.Open Config.Require 'database.url' ; // 'sqlite:data/app.db' // 'postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/shop' // 'mysql://user:password@localhost/shop' Db.Migrate; // database/migrations/ .sql Rows := Db.Query 'select id, name from users where age ? order by name', 18 ; User := Db.QueryOne 'select from users where id = ?', Id ; // nil when none Count := Db.QueryInt 'select count from users', ; Id := Db.Insert 'insert into users name, email values ?, ? ', Name, Email ; Changed := Db.Exec 'update users set name = ? where id = ?', Name, Id ; Tx := Db.BeginTransaction; try Tx.Exec 'update accounts set balance = balance ? where id = ?', Amount, From ; Tx.Exec 'update accounts set balance = balance + ? where id = ?', Amount, To ; Tx.Commit; finally Tx.Free; // rolls back when Commit was not reached end; Rows come back as JSON TJSONArray of TJSONObject, TJSONObject , ready for Res.Json and the J... functions of Pastel.Json; the caller frees them. Values go in as ? and are never pasted into the SQL, so they cannot change it no SQL injection . title: Pastel.Device
text: Pastel.Device The phone's features: share, open, vibrate, notify, pick a file, take a photo, find the place; and the permissions they need. ShareText 'Your appointment: Monday 10:00' ; // Android's share menu ShareFile InvoicePdf ; // the PDF to WhatsApp, mail... OpenUrl 'https://maps.google.com/?q=Istanbul' ; // the browser a file: the app for it Vibrate; // a short buzz Notify 'Sync', '12 appointments came in' ; // in the notification bar Photo := TakePhoto; // '' when cancelled FileName := PickFile 'application/pdf' ; // '' when cancelled if GetLocation Place then Label1.Text := Format '%.5f, %.5f', Place.Latitude, Place.Longitude ; On Android these use the phone's own apps and services through Pastel's activity; the calls that wait TakePhoto, PickFile, GetLocation, RequestPermission keep the app's window alive while they wait. On a computer: OpenUrl opens the browser or the file's app, PickFile shows the open dialog, Notify uses the desktop's notifications on Linux; the others answer False / '' no camera, no place . The calls that wait have a second form that does not: it returns at once and calls a method of yours with the answer — the way for phones: TakePhoto @PhotoTaken ; ... procedure THomeForm.PhotoTaken Sender: TObject; title: Pastel.Dialogs
text: Pastel.Dialogs Dialogs: messages, questions, input, choosing files and folders. ShowMessage 'Saved.' ; if Ask 'Delete this note?' then ... Name := InputBox 'New file', 'Name:', 'notes.txt' ; if OpenFileDialog FileName, 'Text files .txt; .md All files ' then ... if SaveFileDialog FileName, 'Notes .txt' then ... Messages and questions are drawn by Pastel inside the window. The file and folder dialogs are the system's own when it has them Windows; Linux with zenity or kdialog , else Pastel's; UseNativeDialogs := False always takes Pastel's. Test scripts and headless runs get Pastel's, which scripts can click. They wait until the user answered, like Delphi's. Each has a second form that does not wait: it returns at once and calls a method of yours with the answer — the way for phones nothing should wait inside an event there : Ask 'Delete this note?', @DeleteAnswered ; text: Pastel.Http HTTP and HTTPS client. R := HttpGet 'https://api.example.com/users/1' ; if R.Ok then WriteLn R.Body ; Doc := HttpGetJson 'https://api.example.com/users' ; // raises unless 2xx R := HttpPostJson 'https://api.example.com/users', '{"name": "Ali"}' ; HttpDownload 'https://example.com/big.iso', 'big.iso' ; Client := THttpClient.Create 'https://api.example.com/v1' ; Client.BearerToken := Token; Client.Timeout := 10000; Client.Headers := 'Accept Language: tr' ; R := Client.Get '/orders', 'status', 'open', 'page', '2' ; // ?status=open&page=2 R := Client.PostForm '/login', 'user', 'ali', 'pass', 'x' ; Client.Free; HTTPS certificates are checked with the host name , like a browser does. HTTPS PROXY, HTTP PROXY and NO PROXY are followed, including HTTPS through a proxy. OpenSSL 3 and 1.1 both work. title: Pastel.Icons
text: Pastel.Icons Icons: small line drawings for buttons, drawn at any size and in any color, so they are sharp on every screen and right in the dark theme. object SaveButton: TButton Icon = 'save' Text = 'Save' end The built in ones are listed by IconNames. Your own are drawn on a 24 x 24 grid, one command per part, the parts separated by ';': l x1 y1 x2 y2 ... lines through the points o cx cy r a circle f cx cy r a filled circle a dot a cx cy r from to an arc; angles in degrees, 0 = right, 90 = down RegisterIcon 'bell', 'l 6 17 6 10; a 12 10 6 180 360; l 18 10 18 17; l 4 17 20 17; f 12 20 1.5' ; An icon can also be a picture: a PNG, JPEG or BMP file in assets/ or next to the program , drawn in its own colors and fitted into the icon's square: object LogoButton: TButton Icon = 'icons/logo.png' end uses Pastel.Icons; · source: framework/src/pastel.icons.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.icons.pas Contents: DrawIcon drawicon · HasIcon hasicon · RegisterIcon registericon · IconNames iconnames · IconDrawing icondrawing · IsPictureName ispicturename · LoadAppPicture loadapppicture Routines DrawIcon Draws the icon Name in the square X, Y, Size; False when there is no such icon. TMaskEdit Text in a fixed shape: a phone number, an IBAN, a postcode, a tax number. EditMask, like Delphi's: 0 a digit, 9 a digit or nothing, L a letter, l a letter or nothing, A a letter or digit, a the same or nothing, C any character, c any or nothing, what follows in capitals, < in small letters, \ the next one as it is; everything else stays as it is spaces, dashes, brackets . After a ';', 0 leaves those out of Text the digits alone , and after a second ';' the character of the empty places ' ' : EditMask = ' 000 000 00 00' // Text: ' 532 123 45 67' EditMask = 'TR00 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 00;0' // Text: the digits Typing fills the next place and jumps over the fixed characters ; Backspace empties the one before. title: Pastel.Java
text: Pastel.Java Java from Pascal: any class of Android or of the app's own Java files, or of a Java library on a computer , called by its name. "pastel java add android.widget.Toast" writes typed Pascal for the classes you name src/java/javaclasses.pas, like Delphi's Java2OP : JToast.makeText JavaActivity, 'Saved', JToast.LENGTH SHORT .show; Underneath, and for calls of your own, this unit: S := JavaStaticStr 'android.os.Build', 'MODEL', '' ; // a static field N := JavaCallI Obj, 'java.lang.String', 'length', ' I', ; // a method L := JavaNew 'java.util.ArrayList', ' V', ; // a new object The signature is Java's ' Ljava/lang/String;I V' ; Pascal strings become java.lang.String, objects are passed as TJavaObject.Handle. Objects are TJavaObject: a reference Java keeps alive until Pascal no longer uses it freed by itself, like a string . A Java exception becomes an EJavaError with Java's message. Where Java runs: Android the app's own Java Pastel's activity ; any thread. Android's views and Toast want the UI thread: JavaRunOnUiThread. Computers a Java VM started the first time JAVA HOME, else the java of the PATH; PASTEL JVM: the path of libjvm / jvm.dll . Its class path: PASTEL JAVA CLASSPATH, else the project's own Java build/java, written by "pastel java" and java/ beside the program its .jar files : Java libraries in desktop apps. uses Pastel.Java; · source: framework/src/pastel.java.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.java.pas Contents: EJavaError ejavaerror · IJavaRef ijavaref · TJavaObject tjavaobject · JavaAvailable javaavailable · JavaProblem javaproblem · JavaClass javaclass · JavaHasClass javahasclass · JavaNew javanew · JavaCall javacall · JavaCallZ javacallz · JavaCallI javacalli · JavaCallJ javacallj · JavaCallF javacallf · JavaCallD javacalld · JavaCallO javacallo · JavaCallStr javacallstr · JavaStatic javastatic · JavaStaticZ javastaticz · JavaStaticI javastatici · JavaStaticJ javastaticj · JavaStaticF javastaticf · JavaStaticD javastaticd · JavaStaticO javastatico · JavaStaticStr javastaticstr · JavaFieldI javafieldi · JavaFieldJ javafieldj · JavaFieldZ javafieldz · JavaFieldD javafieldd · JavaFieldO javafieldo · JavaFieldStr javafieldstr · JavaString javastring · JavaToString javatostring · JavaWrap javawrap · JavaActivity javaactivity · JavaRunOnUiThread javarunonuithread · JavaImplement javaimplement · JavaCallbackSignature javacallbacksignature · JavaInteger javainteger · JavaInt64 javaint64 · JavaBoolean javaboolean · JavaSingle javasingle · JavaDouble javadouble Types EJavaError IJavaRef function Handle: Pointer TJavaObject A Java object; Pascal keeps it alive while it is used a global reference . title: Pastel.Jwt
text: Pastel.Jwt JSON Web Tokens JWT signed with HS256. Token := JwtSign JObject 'sub', 'ayse', 'role', 'admin' , Secret, 3600 ; // valid 1 hour Claims := JwtVerify Token, Secret ; // EJwtError if forged, changed or expired try WriteLn JStr Claims, 'sub' ; finally Claims.Free; end; Only HS256 HMAC SHA256 with a shared secret is accepted; tokens that ask for another algorithm, or for none, are refused. The secret should be long and random: RandomToken 32 from Pastel.Crypto. uses Pastel.Jwt; · source: framework/src/pastel.jwt.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.jwt.pas Types EJwtError Routines JwtSign Signs Claims and frees them . ExpiresIn: seconds; 0 for no expiry. "iat" and "exp" are added. JwtVerify The claims of a valid token the caller frees them . Leeway: seconds of clock difference allowed between servers.

text: Pastel.Markdown Markdown to HTML, the way GitHub shows it. title: Pastel.Notifications
text: Pastel.Notifications Notifications: a message in the system's notification area, now or at a time, once or again and again; taken back; which one the user tapped. ShowNotification 'Sync', '12 appointments came in' ; ScheduleNotification 'appt 42', 'Appointment', 'Ayşe at 10:00', Start OneHour ; ScheduleNotification 'backup', 'Backup', 'Time for the weekly backup', NextMonday9, riWeekly ; CancelNotification 'appt 42' ; Or as a component on the form TNotificationCenter , with an event for taps: procedure THomeForm.NotificationsNotificationClick Sender: TObject; const AName: string ; begin if AName = 'appt 42' then OpenAppointment 42 ; end; A notification has a name: the same name replaces it shown or scheduled , CancelNotification takes it back. Times are local Now, EncodeDateTime... . Each platform does it its own way, in its own unit: Android Pastel.Notifications.Android: the notification bar; scheduled ones come also when the app is closed and after a restart of the phone AlarmManager; a few minutes late at most while the phone sleeps ; taps are told OnNotificationClick . Needs package.android permissions = "notifications" Android 13 and newer ask the user . Linux Pastel.Notifications.Linux: the desktop's notifications D Bus through gdbus, else notify send . Windows Pastel.Notifications.Windows: a message from the app's icon in the notification area Windows 10 and 11 show it as a toast . macOS Pastel.Notifications.Mac: the Notification Center osascript . title: Pastel.Pages
text: Pastel.Pages HTML pages from templates, in the style of Laravel's Blade. A template is an .html file in views/ views/home.html is 'home', views/shop/list.html is 'shop.list' : @extends 'layout' @section 'title', 'Products' @section 'content' <h1 {{ title }}</h1 @if user.admin <a href="/new" New product</a @endif <ul @forelse products as product <li class="{{ loop.first ? 'first' : '' }}" {{ product.name }} — {{ product.price number:2 }}</li @empty <li No products yet.</li @endforelse </ul @endsection And the code: Res.Html View 'products', JObject 'title', 'Products', 'user', User, 'products', List ; {{ x }} writes x with < & " ' made safe for HTML; {!! x !!} writes it as it is. text: Pastel.Push Push messages: a server sends, the phone shows Firebase Cloud Messaging . object Push: TPushNotifications OnToken = PushToken OnMessage = PushMessage end procedure THomeForm.FormCreate Sender: TObject ; begin RequestPermissions dpNotifications , nil ; // Android 13 and newer ask Push.RequestToken; // OnToken: send it to your server Push.Subscribe 'offers' ; end; procedure THomeForm.PushMessage Sender: TObject; Msg: TPushMessage ; begin if Msg.Opened then // the user tapped its notification ShowAppointment Msg.Data.Values 'appointment' ; end; The app needs Firebase's library and its google services.json: package.android libraries = "com.google.firebase:firebase messaging:24.1.0" permissions = "notifications" pastel package apk then puts Pastel's push service in. title: Pastel.Report

title: Pastel.Service
text: Pastel.Service Long running programs services, daemons . type TBackup = class TService protected procedure Configure C: TConfig ; override; procedure Started; override; procedure Stopping; override; public procedure CheckDisk; procedure Nightly; end; procedure TBackup.Configure C: TConfig ; begin C.SetDefault 'check.interval', '60' ; end; ... begin Service := TBackup.Create AppName, AppVersion ; Service.Every Service.Config.GetFloat 'check.interval' , @Service.CheckDisk, 'check disk' ; Service.DailyAt '03:30', @Service.Nightly, 'nightly backup' ; ExitCode := Service.Run; Service.Free; end. Run loads the settings Pastel.Config , calls Started, runs the jobs until the service is told to stop, then calls Stopping: SIGTERM systemctl stop, docker stop and Ctrl+C stop it cleanly; a second Ctrl+C ends it at once. SIGHUP systemctl reload reads the settings again and calls Reloaded. Under systemd with Type=notify it reports when it is ready and when it stops, and keeps WatchdogSec= happy. A job that raises is logged and runs again next time; the service goes on. uses Pastel.Service; · source: framework/src/pastel.service.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.service.pas Types TServiceJob TService constructor Create const AName: string; const AVersion: string = '' destructor Destroy function Run: Integer Runs until stopped; the exit code for the program. procedure Every Seconds: Double; Job: TJobMethod; const JobName: string = ''; RunAtStart: Boolean = False A job every Seconds; the first run after Seconds, or right at the start. procedure Every Seconds: Double; Job: TJobProc; const JobName: string = ''; RunAtStart: Boolean = False procedure DailyAt const Time: string; Job: TJobMethod; const JobName: string = '' A job once a day at Time '03:30', local time . procedure DailyAt const Time: string; Job: TJobProc; const JobName: string = '' procedure Stop Asks the service to stop from a job, a worker thread, a test . procedure Reload Asks it to read the settings again, as SIGHUP does. function Wait Ms: Integer : Boolean Sleeps up to Ms milliseconds; returns False at once when the service is stopping. Long jobs use it instead of Sleep. property Name: string property Version: string property Config: TConfig property IsStopping: Boolean property StateDir: string A folder for the service's own files: $STATE DIRECTORY under systemd StateDirectory= , else ./data. Created when first used. Other types type TJobMethod = procedure type TJobProc = procedure Routines NextDailyRun When a daily job at Time 'HH:MM' runs next, seen from Now. NotifySystemd Tells systemd about the service "READY=1", "STOPPING=1", "STATUS=..." . Does nothing outside systemd.

title: Pastel.Sync
text: Pastel.Sync Data that works offline and is synchronized with a server: the desktop or phone keeps its own SQLite file, works without a network, and exchanges the changes with the server when it can. Store := TSyncStore.Create TDatabase.Open 'sqlite:shop.db' , True ; Store.AddTable 'customers', 'name varchar 200 not null, ' + 'phone varchar 50 not null default '''', notes text' ; Store.OnCheck := @CheckRecord; // raise ESyncInvalid for wrong values Store.CreateTables; Id := Store.Save 'customers', JObject 'name', 'Ayşe Yılmaz' ; // a new id; checked Rows := Store.List 'customers', 'lower name like ?', '%ayşe%' , 'name' ; Store.Delete 'customers', Id ; // marked, so the deletion travels too R := SyncWithServer Store, 'https://shop.example.com', ApiKey, LastSync ; // the client AddSyncRoute Web, ServerStore ; // the server Pastel.SyncWeb : POST /api/sync How it works: every record gets its id where it is made 16 random characters, so computers never clash , and updated at, the time of its last change UTC, sortable as text . A client marks what it changes dirty , sends it, and takes what the server got from others since its last sync. When a record was changed on both sides, the newer change wins; sending the same records twice changes nothing. Records are never really deleted, only marked deleted = 1 . The server's clock decides what is new for a client synced at , so clocks of the computers may be wrong. The salon example examples/salon core is built on it. uses Pastel.Sync; · source: framework/src/pastel.sync.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.sync.pas Contents: ESyncInvalid esyncinvalid · TSyncResult tsyncresult · TSyncStore tsyncstore · SyncStamp syncstamp · NewSyncId newsyncid · SyncWithServer syncwithserver · AnswerSync answersync Types ESyncInvalid TSyncResult Sent: Integer Received: Integer TSyncStore constructor Create ADb: TDatabase; OwnsDb: Boolean = False destructor Destroy procedure AddTable const Name: string; const Columns: string A table that is synchronized: its columns as SQL, without the ones every table gets id, updated at, synced at, dirty, deleted . procedure CreateTables The tables, when they are missing. function Tables: TStringArray function Fields const Table: string : TStringArray function Save const Table: string; Data: TJSONObject : string Checks and stores a record: a new one without "id", else the one with this id values not given keep theirs . Returns the id. function Get const Table: string; const Id: string : TJSONObject One record, nil when there is none or it is deleted ; the caller frees it. procedure Delete const Table: string; const Id: string function List const Table: string; const Where: string = ''; const Params: array of const; const OrderBy: string = '' : TJSONArray The records that are not deleted. Where: more conditions 'status = ?' , OrderBy: 'name' default: updated at . The caller frees it. function List const Table: string : TJSONArray function Count const Table: string : Integer function Changes const Since: string; Dirty: Boolean : TJSONObject function Apply Data: TJSONObject : Integer Takes records from the other side; returns how many were newer and stored. procedure MarkSent Data: TJSONObject After the server took them: not dirty any more unless changed again meanwhile . function Pending: Integer The number of records waiting to be sent. property Db: TDatabase property IsServer: Boolean True on the server: Save and Apply stamp records with the server's clock, so clients get them on their next sync. property OnCheck: TSyncCheckEvent Checks a record before it is stored also records that come with a sync : raise ESyncInvalid with a message for the user. Other types type TSyncCheckEvent = procedure Table: string; Data: TJSONObject Routines SyncStamp The current time as records are stamped: '2026 11 01T09:30:00.123000Z'; always larger than the one before, also in the same millisecond. NewSyncId A new id: 16 random characters. SyncWithServer A client's sync: sends what change

title: Pastel.TrueType
text: Pastel.TrueType TrueType fonts in plain Pascal: reads a .ttf or the first font of a .ttc and draws its glyphs with anti aliasing, without FreeType. Pastel uses FreeType when it is there it also hints small text ; this unit is used where it is not: always on Android, and on a desktop without the FreeType library. Outlines with straight lines and quadratic curves the "glyf" table are supported, simple and composite glyphs, the cmap formats 4 and 12 and kerning pairs of the "kern" table. text: Pastel.Updater The app updates itself. if CheckForUpdate 'https://example.com/shop/update.json', '1.4.2', Update then if Ask 'Version ' + Update.Version + ' is there. Update now?' then begin F := DownloadUpdate Update ; // checked against its SHA 256 InstallUpdate F ; // the installer runs, the app ends end; The file on your server pastel update manifest writes it from dist/ : { "version": "1.5.0", "notes": "Faster sync", "files": { "windows x86 64": { "url": "https://.../shop 1.5.0 setup.exe", "sha256": "..." }, "linux x86 64": { "url": "https://.../shop 1.5.0 x86 64.AppImage", "sha256": "..." }, "android": { "url": "https://.../shop 1.5.0.apk", "sha256": "..." } } } InstallUpdate: Windows runs the installer silently, it starts the app again ; an AppImage is replaced and started again; a .deb opens in the system's installer; Android asks the user to install the .apk package.android permissions = "install updates" . title: Pastel.Web
text: Pastel.Web HTTP server for web APIs and sites. Web := TWebServer.Create 8080 ; Web.Get '/hello', @Hello ; Web.Get '/users/:id', @GetUser ; Web.Post '/users', @CreateUser ; Web.Static '/', 'public' ; // files: public/index.html, public/app.css, ... Web.Health '/health', AppVersion ; Web.Start; // serves in the background until Web.Stop procedure GetUser Req: TWebRequest; Res: TWebResponse ; var User: TJSONObject; begin User := FindUser Req.ParamInt 'id' ; if User = nil then raise EWebError.Create 404, 'no user with this id' ; Res.Json User ; end; Requests are handled at the same time in several threads: what handlers share must be protected TCriticalSection or be read only. Errors become JSON answers: EWebError 404, 'no user' 404 {"error": "no user"}; a bad JSON body 400; any other exception 500, logged, with the message in the answer only in debug builds. uses Pastel.Web; title: Pastel.WebImages
text: Pastel.WebImages Pictures from the web: posters, logos, avatars. B := WebImage 'https://example.com/poster.jpg' ; // nil while it comes if B < nil then C.DrawBitmap B, X, Y, W, H ; Four threads fetch them what is asked last, first: what is on the screen now ; the window paints again when one comes. They are kept in memory the ones used least go: MaxWebImages and in a cache folder, made smaller on the way WebImageMaxSide , so a list of thousands of posters stays light. A bitmap given by WebImage is for drawing at once: do not keep it. TImage.Url and TTileView use it. title: Pastel.WebSocket
text: Pastel.WebSocket WebSockets: a connection that stays open, messages both ways chat, live updates, notifications from the server . On a server Pastel.Web : Chat := TWebSockets.Create; Chat.OnMessage := @ChatMessage; Web.WebSocket '/chat', Chat ; // behind RequireJwt, RateLimit... like routes procedure TApi.ChatMessage Socket: TWebSocket; const Text: string ; begin Chat.Broadcast Socket.Claim 'name' + ': ' + Text ; end; In an app, or a program talking to a server: Client := TWebSocketClient.Create; Client.OnMessage := @Received; // on the app's thread, like a button's click Client.BearerToken := Token; Client.Connect 'wss://api.example.com/chat' ; Client.Send 'hello' ; Text messages are UTF 8 strings; binary ones TBytes OnBinary . title: Pastel.Workers
text: Pastel.Workers Background work: a thread safe queue and a pool of worker threads. Mail := TWorkerPool.Create 'mail', 4, @SendMail ; // 4 threads Mail.Submit JObject 'to', 'ayse@example.com' .AsJSON ; ... Mail.Free; // takes no new work, finishes what is queued, then stops procedure TApi.SendMail const Msg: string ; begin ... // runs in one of the worker threads end; Messages are strings often JSON , so nothing is shared between threads by accident. An exception in a handler is logged and counted; the worker goes on with the next message. TMessageQueue on its own passes messages between any threads. uses Pastel.Workers; · source: framework/src/pastel.workers.pas ../../framework/src/pastel.workers.pas Types TMessageQueue First in, first out; any number of threads may push and pop. constructor Create MaxCount: Integer = 0 MaxCount 0: no limit destructor Destroy function Push const Msg: string : Boolean False when the queue is closed or full function Pop out Msg: string; TimeoutMs: Integer = 1 : Boolean waits up to TimeoutMs 1: until there is a message or the queue is closed ; False after the time, or when closed and empty procedure Close no new messages; Pop still returns the ones queued function Count: Integer property Closed: Boolean TWorkerPool constructor Create const AName: string; Count: Integer; Handler: TWorkHandler; MaxQueue: Integer = 0 constructor Create const AName: string; Count: Integer; Handler: TWorkHandlerProc; MaxQueue: Integer = 0 destructor Destroy Stop, then free function Submit const Msg: string : Boolean queue a message; False after Stop or when the queue is full procedure Stop WarnAfterMs: Integer = 30000 no new work; waits until the queued work is done a warning in the log when it takes longer than WarnAfterMs function WaitIdle TimeoutMs: Integer = 30000 : Boolean waits until the queue is empty and no worker is busy; False after TimeoutMs property Name: string property Pending: Integer property Processed: Integer property Failed: Integer TBackgroundTask Long work of a window app a slow query, a download that would make the window wait: Work runs on a thread of its own, then Done on the main thread; the window stays alive meanwhile. RunInBackground @LoadRows, @RowsLoaded ; procedure TMainForm.LoadRows Sender: TObject ; // its own thread: no controls here begin TBackgroundTask Sender .Data := Db.Query ... ; end; procedure TMainForm.RowsLoaded Sender: TObject ; // the main thread begin with TBackgroundTask Sender do if Error < '' then ShowMessage Error else Grid.LoadJson TJSONArray Data ; end; The task frees itself after Done forget it there ; Cancel before that: Done is not called and Data is freed the work itself runs to its end . constructor Create AWork: TNotifyEvent; ADone: TNotifyEvent; AData: TObject; ATag: PtrInt procedure Cancel property Error: string the message of the exception Work raised; '' when it went well property Cancelled: Boolean property Data: TObject what Work leaves for Done Done frees it or keeps it property Tag: PtrInt Other types type TWorkHandler = procedure Msg: string type TWorkHandlerProc = procedure Msg: string Routines RunInBackground Data: what Work needs and leaves its results in , there before Work starts.
